stories.headline: NFL suspends Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game for spitting
stories.summary: The NFL has suspended Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game after cameras captured him spitting toward Raiders players on Sunday.
stories.body:
The NFL has suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay after cameras captured him spitting toward Las Vegas Raiders players on Sunday.

The league said in a statement that Gardner-Johnson violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."

Barring an appeal, Gardner-Johnson will miss the Bills' Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo is on a bye this week. Any appeal would be heard by Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera or James Thrash, who are jointly appointed and paid by the NFL and the NFL Players Association.

Bills coach Joe Brady said Monday there'll be no further punishment for Gardner-Johnson beyond the league's suspension. Brady remained committed to Gardner-Johnson as a starter when he's eligible to return from suspension in Week 9.

"C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with. He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. ... We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line."

Brady preferred to keep the conversations between he, Gardner-Johnson and the team private. Even given Gardner-Johnson's reputation for toeing and crossing the line, Brady said he has no problem with Gardner-Johnson's personality or character fit within the organization, saying he doesn't need all of his players to behave in one prescribed way.

"We brought him here for a reason," Brady added. "He knows he has to play better, and he knows he has to be better for this team. Just like everybody else we've got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes."

Gardner-Johnson was ejected from Sunday's game after spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum shortly before halftime. He apologized to his teammates after the Bills' 33-30 victory and said he needed to be a better veteran moving forward.

The incident came after a play in which Gardner-Johnson and Bowers jawed, but Gardner-Johnson said there wasn't a specific incitement that sparked the flagrant act.

"We were just arguing and talking," Gardner-Johnson told reporters. "It was nothing negative. He ain't do nothing to me. It was just in the heat of the game arguing and talking s---. That gesture isn't warranted."

Said Bowers: "I don't even know. Just talking a little bit and then ... I don't know."

Later Sunday, in a social media post, Gardner-Johnson formally apologized "to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me."

"My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game."

Referee Shawn Smith said via a pool report that umpire Tra Blake witnessed Gardner-Johnson spit toward Bowers, triggering his ejection. This was the second time in two weeks that Gardner-Johnson registered a 15-yard penalty and the first time he had been ejected from a game since 2024.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Messi's Inter Miami moving up, Nashville still No.1
stories.summary: Nashville are very much still the team to beat, but Inter Miami, St. Louis City SC and Philly are hot on their heels in our latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

Nashville clocked four shots on target in a 1-1 draw with San Jose, but neither team reached higher than a 0.73 xG (and it wasn't Nashville). The draw might be a disappointment for fans ready for the team to clinch the Shield, but Nashville can secure it with a win in Montreal, and with four games to go, it will need just eight points to set a single-season points record to boot.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 3

Don't look now, but the star-studded Herons have found their feet with a three-game win streak after the international break. In a 3-1 win against Atlanta, Messi scored twice in the space of four minutes, bringing him to seven goals in their past six games.

3. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

St. Louis picked up its first loss since May 3 in a 3-2 defeat to the Loons. With its 19-game unbeaten streak snapped, STL has fallen short of the undefeated record but could still grab first place in the West with a strong four-game finish.

4. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 4

Philly scored first and last in a 2-2 draw with Charlotte, which maintained a 15-game undefeated streak started after the World Cup. That said, the Union snapped their eight-game run of wins that was briefly kept alive with a midweek win against Chicago.

5. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 6

The Whitecaps still have a slim four-point lead at the top of the Western Conference after beating Austin FC 2-1. It wasn't the toughest competition or the best display, but Vancouver is still on track to greet the playoffs with a comfortable position in the West.

6. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

Still one of the stronger teams in the East, the Fire faced off against two of their fellow East Coast contenders (Philly and New England) and came up short in both games. They'll have notes for the postseason after Saturday's 1-0 defeat to the Revs.

7. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 7

After conceding first from the penalty spot, Charlotte scored twice to claim a 2-1 lead before conceding a final goal to Bruno Damiani. It salvaged a point with a 2-2 draw, but the team has just one win (and two defeats) in its past four games as it vies for a better chance at home-field advantage in the postseason.

8. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

LAFC are undefeated in two games after limping their way to a 1-1 draw against NYCFC. Leo Walta's first-half goal from a free kick was a thing of beauty (his first for the club in just his third match), but they didn't capitalize enough in the final third to come away with more than a draw.

9. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 10

After a slight stumble with defeats against Philly and the Revs, Orlando is undefeated in three games after beating D.C. United 4-1. In the 22nd minute, Antoine Griezmann finished off a crafty set of passes with a chipped assist to Martin Ojeda, who rewarded the team effort with a backheel bicycle kick worthy of an award.

10. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 9

The Sounders were soaring into the postseason on a four-game win streak before stumbling against FC Dallas, then needing a second-half goal from 20-year-old Sebastian Gomez to level the score 1-1 against last-in-the-East CF Montreal. With a few interesting tests ahead, they'll need to recover quickly if they are to avoid starting the playoffs in the wild-card round.

11. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 11

After Mateusz Bogusz scored a 94th-minute penalty, Houston was on its way to its first win in six games until Petar Musa scored a response from the spot in the 11th minute of stoppage time. With that, the Dynamo have four draws in their past five games and are comfortably in the playoff places though still short of home-field advantage.

12. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 12

Matt Turner's six saves paid dividends in a slim victory over Chicago, as Carles Gil set up Matt Polster for his second goal of the season to make the difference in a 1-0 win over Chicago.

13. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

Petar Musa's penalty in the 11th minute of stoppage time salvaged a 2-2 draw against Houston, securing Dallas' fourth point in two games after it beat Seattle 1-0 in midweek.

14. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 13

Cincinnati has three defeats in four games and is winless in its past two after losing this weekend's Hell is Real Derby. The club is in the final wild-card position in the East and hanging on to its playoff chances by the skin of its teeth, with three heavy hitters -- Miami, Philly and Nashville -- waiting in the last four games.

15. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 17

The Western Conference is tightly packed with the playoffs looming, but San Jose still hasn't lost since August and extended that run with a 1-1 draw against first-place Nashville. For those following, that's three 1-1 draws in three games for the Quakes, and four draws in the past five outings.

16. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 16

Matt Freese made two strong saves but also has a bit of egg on his face after standing stationary on Leo Walta's first-half goal from a free kick. Andres Perea took the team on his shoulders with a second-half goal to seal the point.

17. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 15

The Red Bulls generated enough to get a result in a 2-0 defeat to Toronto but couldn't break through despite outpacing them in the final third. With three defeats in four games, that result could haunt them as they finished the weekend in the wild-card spot, but dead even with Toronto (one spot short of the playoffs) on points.

18. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 18

The Galaxy's two-game faceoff against their fellow SoCal sides started with a draw against a 2-2 draw against a limited San Diego. They've got a slim grasp on their playoff spot with LAFC up next.

19. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 20

Minnesota's first win since Aug. 22 came against a team that hadn't lost since May. The Loons came back from an early two-goal deficit to claim a 3-2 win capped off by an 88th-minute goal from Marcus Caldeira, who capitalized on a counterattack to collect his seventh goal in 12 games.

20. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 19

Nicolas Hansen's four saves were needed in a 0-0 game against Portland that saw the Rapids slightly outmatched in big chances as they hung on to their wild-card spot for dear life with four draws in five games.

21. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 22

Patrick Schulte's seven saves did a lot of work in a 2-0 win against their Ohio rivals, as FC Cincinnati crumbled without registering a single save in a match that saw the Crew outshot 23-3 and 7-2 on target.

22. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 24

Toronto's 2-0 win over RBNY has it undefeated in three games as it stares down the home stretch with a playoff spot in reach. The club finished the weekend in 10th place, one spot short of the wild card places, but even on points with the two teams above. Upcoming games with Columbus, D.C. and Atlanta mean Toronto still has some control over its postseason destiny.

23. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 21

RSL is in a race against themselves to break into the playoff positions (they finished the weekend one spot short in the West). After beating SKC 3-1, they've got just one loss in their past four games and secured two wins -- their first victories since the World Cup. Morgan Guilavogui's brace of goals (his first since August) made the difference.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 23

San Diego's 2-2 draw with the Galaxy is its fourth draw in five games. They've come against respectable playoff teams, but San Diego is going to need more if it is to launch itself into the postseason over the final few games.

25. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 25

The Timbers have a habit of doing the work to get more from a result but somehow walking away short of three points. In a 0-0 draw against Colorado, they couldn't break through in the final third, and they will struggle to break into the playoffs with tough tests ahead -- Charlotte and Houston at home, St. Louis and Austin away -- to close out the season.

26. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 26

With only SKC keeping them above last place in the West, Verde fans can take pride in small victories such as limiting first-place Vancouver in a slim 2-1 defeat.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

Sean Johnson's three saves did their best, but United suffered their second 4-1 loss in three games, this time against Orlando. The good news? They beat RBNY in between and can technically still make the playoffs -- but so can everyone else.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

The bad news is Atlanta lost again. The good news is it managed to stop Lionel Messi from getting a hat trick in the 3-1 loss to Inter Miami.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

In their first match since officially getting eliminated from the playoffs, SKC have lost again, this time against RSL.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Montreal is on the cusp of being the first team in the East eliminated from the playoffs after drawing against Seattle 1-1, and it could have the honor of being eliminated by Nashville on the same night that club clinches the Shield. In between: the Canadian Championship final.

stories.body:
The NBA offseason is over, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season long, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Oct. 19

Curry practiced, expected to play Wednesday

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr told reporters that Stephen Curry practiced this morning and is expected to play in Wednesday night's game against the Los Angeles Lakers.

Mavericks waive center Powell
The Dallas Mavericks waived Dwight Powell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Powell had spent the last 12 seasons with the franchise.

Hoop Collective: The biggest questions in the NBA's Atlantic Division
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to discuss the NBA's Atlantic Division with ESPN analyst and radio host Alan Hahn. The trio covers how the New York Knicks will defend their title, what changes to expect with the Philadelphia 76ers and whether the Boston Celtics' big moves will pay off. Hahn on how to keep Karl-Anthony Towns happy this season: "I can tell you from talking to him, on-the-side conversations, not in interviews, but [him] almost pleading because, people would ask him about shots. 'You only took four shots in the first half. What happened?' And all that stuff.

"And it was one time I was walking away and he kind of grabbed me. He's like, 'It's not about shots. I don't care about shots.' He said, 'I just [like] being involved.' He's like, 'I love to pass the ball. I just want to help my teammates.' And so when they moved more in that Atlanta series, which turned everything into him being a hub of the offense, he was the happiest. I'm telling you this is not propaganda, he really was. He was happy because he loves to pass. And if you see the flair with the different ways he passes the basketball and the smile on his face, he wears 32, his father's number, but it's also Magic Johnson. And he has told that story many times. He loves that.

"So what Windy's saying, that's literally the truth. If you want to keep him happy, keep him involved and everything else will figure itself out."

Windhorst on Stephen Curry's injury update: "I don't think that they're concerned that this knee is going to be devastating, but they've just got to protect him.

"So he walks off and after the events, [coach] Steve Kerr said that it was actually his right ankle, not his knee, and that he expected to be fine. So that happened, but still a little bit alarming. And you could tell by the way Steph acted, it didn't look like an ankle, but obviously Steph, anything with a Steph ankle, he's going to be sensitive to that, too."

Oct. 18

Wallace lands extension with Thunder
Oklahoma City Thunder All-Defensive guard Cason Wallace has agreed to a five-year, $139 million rookie-scale contract extension, his agents told ESPN's Shams Charania. Wallace, who will turn 23 next month, led the NBA in total steals and deflections last season and has ranked third in steals per game in each of the past two seasons, according to ESPN Research.

Kram: Grading the Wallace extension

Ighodaro signs multi-year deal to stay in Phoenix
Phoenix Suns center Oso Ighodaro has agreed to a three-year, $29 million contract extension through the 2030-31 season, his agent Erika Ruiz of Primera Sports told ESPN.

The Suns will pick up Ighodaro's $2.5M team option for 2027-28, so the extension starts in 2028 and runs through 2031 for the franchise's 2024 second-round pick.

Simmons tears Achilles, out for the season
Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons tore an Achilles tendon at practice Sunday, sources told ESPN. Simmons, the 2016 No. 1 pick whom the Kings signed this offseason, was readying to play his first regular-season game since 2024-2025.

Oct. 16

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

Read more: Which NBA deals will get done? Bobby Marks' biggest extension decisions to watch

Obviously they needed some lottery luck, but Tre Johnson, Kyshawn George are interesting players. I don't know quite what to make out of Bilal Coulibaly at this point or Bub Carrington. But then, [AJ] Dybantsa, he needs to be the face of the franchise sooner rather than later.

"They've got some interesting pieces in place, but the guys at the top of their salary structure to me are: Trae's a bad contract and AD's a bad situation."

Eubanks suffers torn pectoral muscle
New York Knicks reserve center Drew Eubanks has a torn pectoral muscle and will be sidelined for an extended period of time, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The Knicks will waive Eubanks, who was competing for a roster spot.

Clippers waive Christie

Brian is joined by ESPN's Vincent Goodwill and Tim MacMahon to preview the NBA's Central Division, including the biggest questions facing the five teams. Is this another make-or-break season for the Cleveland Cavaliers? Will the Detroit Pistons repeat their 2025-26 success? Windhorst on whether the Cavaliers can improve their roster: "Jarrett Allen is the guy that they would have to do something with. And the thing about it is that they can't trade Jarrett Allen because you'd need a franchise center. And that means Evan Mobley would probably have to be your franchise center.

"First off, if you're trading Jarrett Allen, are you upgrading at center for trading Jarrett Allen? No, you're probably upgrading somewhere else and you're asking Evan Mobley to play center. And Evan Mobley has not proven, even though a lot of people believe that he would be at his best playing full-time stretch center, [he can do that]. That's not something they've been able to get Evan to do consistently well. But that's the move that they have. The move that they have if they have to do something is to look at Jarrett Allen.

"But we'll see how that plays out. The Cavs are in a tough spot in that they are going to be expected to improve on last season, which the pathway to improve on a conference final season, it's a narrow path. And they're doing it in a much more competitive Eastern Conference landscape."

ESPN reporter Vincent Goodwill wrote Friday about why the Detroit Pistons and big man Jalen Duren -- who engaged in a contract stalemate this offseason before Duren got a five-year, $200 million contract -- needed each other. In that piece, Goodwill dropped a nugget on other players Detroit explored adding since its season ended:

The Pistons inquired about trading for Kawhi Leonard and Kevin Durant this offseason, according to league sources, and were positioned to offer Austin Reaves a big free agent contract if the Los Angeles Lakers opened the door. None of that materialized.
The Pistons had heard Leonard wasn't interested in coming to Detroit amid the Clippers' cap-circumvention scandal, per league sources, and the Rockets weren't willing to engage on Durant despite the close relationship he shares with Cunningham. "We're in a position now [as opposed to past seasons] where we can be thinking of development. Not just for Yaxel, but our whole group. We are not in the [championship] conversation. Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey weekly pickups: Add these available forwards on productive lines
stories.summary: Begin your fantasy hockey week with forwards, defensemen, goalies and streamers to add to your lineup.
stories.body:
Two games on Wednesday and two games on Friday. Daily lineup managers, this is the week to work the bench, with the scoring period from Oct. 19 to Oct. 25 packing 48 games around some very quiet nights.

The Anaheim Ducks, Colorado Avalanche, Minnesota Wild, San Jose Sharks and Toronto Maple Leafs get four games apiece, and the Wild have the best schedules of the week for both skaters and goalies. The Buffalo Sabres, Columbus Blue Jackets, Calgary Flames, Chicago Blackhawks and Washington Capitals are stuck at two.

The Avalanche are the best streaming target in leagues with weekly transactions, with four games and an average of only 10 other teams in action on the same nights. Watch for afternoon puck drops at 1 p.m. on Saturday and 3 p.m. on Sunday.

Every Monday, we'll mine the waiver wire for lesser-rostered performers who have the potential to help fantasy teams in a variety of leagues. We'll also present several strong streaming candidates for the immediate week ahead.

More: Rankings | Most added/dropped | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | Cheat sheet | Weekly picks | Sign up

Forwards

Dylan Strome, C, Washington Capitals (1.71 FPPG, 33.3% available): Strome has moved to a Capitals top line with Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, and he's kept his spot on the top power-play unit. The timing is the catch: a two-game week against a tough slate makes this a long-term add rather than a play for this week. Two points in his past three games and last season's 1.62 FPPG suggest the floor holds either way.

Jack Quinn, RW, Buffalo Sabres (2.19 FPPG, 58.0% available): Quinn has five points in his past three games, and the underlying numbers back up the surge: his line with Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson is 6-1 on goals at 5-on-5 across 95 minutes, with 66.9% of the shot attempts. Add a regular spot on the top power-play unit and he's a well-rounded add for the long haul. Just don't expect much this week, with only two games against the toughest slate for top-six forwards.

Viktor Arvidsson, RW, Detroit Red Wings (1.91 FPPG, 74.2% available): Lining up with Dylan Larkin and Lucas Raymond is a nice place to be, even if the trio is 1-3 on goals at 5-on-5. They're carrying 55.8% of the shot attempts, so the goals should even out, and Arvidsson already has three power-play points from his spot on the top unit. A western road trip through Seattle, Vancouver and Calgary helps with those opponents combining for the sixth-friendliest slate for top-six forwards.

Alex Laferriere, C/RW, Los Angeles Kings (2.00 FPPG, 40.7% available): Laferriere has yet to cash in on the power play, but he's on the ice for 74% of the Kings' time with the extra skater, and the top unit is generating 3.92 shot attempts per two minutes. Those points should come. In the meantime, 19 hits through six games give him a floor in leagues that count them, and his C/RW eligibility adds lineup flexibility.

Will Cuylle, LW, New York Rangers (1.72 FPPG, 35.0% available): Cuylle has been cashing in on a line with Eeli Tolvanen and Noah Laba, and he's matching last season's 1.73 FPPG almost exactly. That consistency is the selling point, since the trio is getting outshot (45.7% of the attempts) despite a 3-1 edge on goals. The week ahead helps: the Ducks, Maple Leafs and Ottawa Senators combine for the seventh-friendliest slate for top-six forwards.

See also:

Joel Eriksson Ek, C, Minnesota Wild (1.60 FPPG, 30.8% available)

Boone Jenner, C/LW, Washington Capitals (2.14 FPPG, 78.2% available)

Mason McTavish, C, St. Louis Blues (2.44 FPPG, 40.7% available)

Brayden Schenn, C/LW, New York Islanders (1.61 FPPG, 76.4% available)

Ryan Leonard, RW, Washington Capitals (1.93 FPPG, 66.6% available)

Elias Lindholm, C, Boston Bruins (1.66 FPPG, 67.7% available)

Defense

Seth Jones, D, Florida Panthers (2.31 FPPG, 30.1% available): Jones has heated up in a hurry, with seven points in his past three games, and only 14 skaters have more fantasy points across the past two weeks. With Aleksander Barkov out until at least late November, the Panthers need offense from somewhere, and Jones is a fixture on the top power-play unit with five points on the advantage already. He's still available in nearly a third of leagues, and that shouldn't last.

Neal Pionk, D, Winnipeg Jets (2.12 FPPG, 72.0% available): With Josh Morrissey out until at least Nov. 1, Pionk has stepped into top-pair minutes and the top power-play unit for the Jets. Five points in his past three games are the flashy part, but the real foundation is 24-plus minutes a night and a steady stream of hits and blocks, which account for nearly half of his fantasy points. He's available in nearly three-quarters of leagues.

Travis Sanheim, D, Philadelphia Flyers (1.70 FPPG, 31.2% available): Injuries to Rasmus Ristolainen and Cam York have pushed Sanheim's ice time to a staggering 27:32 per game over his past three, and 21 blocked shots have done most of the fantasy work. He's not on the power play and his pair with Oliver Bonk is 0-4 on goals at 5-on-5, so this is a play for leagues that reward blocks. Two of the Flyers' three games land on light nights.

See also:

Alexandre Carrier, D, Montreal Canadiens (1.70 FPPG, 93.3% available)

Martin Fehervary, D, Washington Capitals (1.90 FPPG, 71.4% available)

Tyler Kleven, D, Ottawa Senators (2.03 FPPG, 78.3% available)

Justin Faulk, D, Detroit Red Wings (1.51 FPPG, 34.2% available)

Goaltenders

Jet Greaves, G, Columbus Blue Jackets (2.35 FPP60, 49.5% available): Cam Talbot has taken three of the past seven starts, but Greaves still holds the edge in the Blue Jackets crease after posting 2.06 FPPG across 55 games last season. This week is the downside: only two games, and neither is a top-10 matchup for goalies.

Dylan Garand, G, New York Rangers (4.20 FPP60, 45.4% available): With Igor Shesterkin out for the season and Joonas Korpisalo on IR until at least Nov. 9, Garand's only competition is Spencer Martin, who hasn't started any of the Rangers' past 10 games. Three wins and a .927 save percentage through six games is a solid opening, and he's still available in nearly half of leagues. None of this week's three opponents offers a particularly favorable matchup for goalies, but volume is the draw.

Lukas Dostal, G, Anaheim Ducks (0.49 FPP60, 58.7% available): It's been a rough start for Dostal, and that's exactly why he's sitting on the wire in most leagues. The schedule makes a strong case for buying low anyway. The Ducks have four games and the second-best goalie schedule of the week, including the Rangers and Devils, both favorable matchups for fantasy goalies. Even a share of that crease is worth chasing.

See also:

Pyotr Kochetkov, G, Carolina Hurricanes (4.08 FPP60, 49.6% available)

Devon Levi, G, Edmonton Oilers (2.50 FPP60, 68.7% available)

Jacob Markstrom, G, Florida Panthers (2.43 FPP60, 38.4% available)

Juuse Saros, G, Nashville Predators (1.78 FPP60, 31.6% available)

Short-term streamers

Gabriel Landeskog, LW, Colorado Avalanche (1.74 FPPG, 73.2% available): The Avalanche are this week's top team for streaming, and Landeskog is an easy way in. He's on the second line with Nazem Kadri and Brock Nelson, has three points in his past three games and chips in hits. With three of Colorado's four games on light nights, he can slot into a daily lineup with little competition.

Blake Coleman, RW, Minnesota Wild (1.46 FPPG, 43.0% available): Coleman has gone quiet with no points in his past three games, but the schedule is too good to ignore. The Wild play four times, and their opponents combine for the friendliest slate of the week for top-six forwards, with two bottom-10 penalty kills on the trip. Now skating on the second line with Ryan Hartman and Bobby Brink, he also adds hits (18 so far) to cover the quiet nights.

Jonas Brodin, D, Minnesota Wild (1.49 FPPG, 96.3% available): Brodin is almost purely a blocked-shots play, with 22 of them making up nearly all of his 13.4 fantasy points. But he's skating 86% of his even-strength time next to Quinn Hughes while Jared Spurgeon and Brock Faber are out, and the Wild's four opponents combine for the fourth-friendliest slate for top-four defenders. That pairing may not survive Spurgeon's return, so treat this as a one-week deep-league rental.

Josh Manson, D, Colorado Avalanche (1.77 FPPG, 74.3% available): Like Landeskog, Manson is a vehicle for the Avalanche schedule: four games, three of them on light nights, against opponents who combine for the third-friendliest slate for top-four defenders. Playing on the top pair with Brent Burns, he gets most of his value from hits and blocks, which account for more than half of his fantasy points.

Alexander Wennberg, C, San Jose Sharks (1.06 FPPG, 86.0% available): Wennberg's slow start is a far cry from last season's 1.75 FPPG, but the role points to a turnaround. He's up to 21-plus minutes a night over his past three games, including more than five minutes on the top power-play unit, and his new line with Tyler Toffoli and Mason Marchment is controlling 61.9% of the shot attempts. The Sharks' four opponents combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-six forwards.

John Gibson, G, Detroit Red Wings (-0.61 FPP60, 41.2% available): The Red Wings have the third-best goalie schedule of the week, and all three of their games are top-10 matchups for fantasy goalies, including the Canucks (second) and Flames (first). With no bad draws on the slate, whichever games Gibson gets should be good ones.

stories.headline: Champions League Power Rankings before MD3: Who's No. 1?
stories.summary: It's time for the UEFA Champions League! It has been about six weeks since our last check-in, but our panel of experts and voters will rank the top 10 teams in the field. Where does your club rank?
stories.body:
The 2026-27 European club season is in full swing as we approach November, and despite a three-week international break putting teams on pause, we have a sufficient body of work to judge heading into Matchday 3 of the UEFA Champions League.

So far in Europe's top tournament, nine teams are a perfect 2-0-0 to open their campaign, though some of those teams -- Stuttgart! Real Betis! -- are flying higher than their league form should suggest. That said, there are several juggernauts crowded at the top end of the table and some true heavyweight clashes ahead this week, as Barcelona visit back-to-back champions Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday and Bayern Munich welcome Premier League champions Arsenal to the Allianz Arena on Wednesday.

What will it do to the standings?

Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.

UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 3

1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN

- Previous rank: 1

- Games since MD1: defeated Brest 1-0, defeated Marseille 2-1, defeated Le Mans 3-1, defeated Man City 4-2, defeated Strasbourg 3-1

- MD3 opponent: vs. Barcelona, Tuesday

Luis Enrique's side is a notorious slow starter domestically, by its own admission, but after two draws and a defeat to open the season, PSG well and truly seem back on track now. Since a 6-1 rout of Slovan Bratislava on UCL Matchday 1, they've won every game with a rotating cast of characters. Summer signing Ferran Torres from Barcelona has seven goals already, and 10 different players have found the net across the team's 11 games in all competitions.

Young arrivals Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche have also embraced Luis Enrique's style of play, and while PSG do look a little wobbly at the back with the veteran Marquinhos losing a step and goalie Matvey Safonov also fallible, they have the attacking prowess to make that less of an issue. Our voters certainly aren't concerned: with 17 of 20 first-place votes, they are our consensus top team.

2. BARCELONA

- Previous rank: 4

- Games since MD1: defeated Levante 4-2, defeated Racing Santander 7-2, defeated Sevilla 3-1, defeated Getafe 3-0, defeated Galatasaray 4-1, defeated Real Betis 5-2

- MD3 opponent: at PSG, Tuesday

Hansi Flick's side began the season at pace with 17 goals in its first four LaLiga games prior to a 5-1 shellacking of Feyenoord to open its Champions League campaign. What have Barca done since? Six games, six wins and 26 more goals scored. It's an alarming speed, but so far, as we head into the chillier months, they are superb -- our voters agreed, with Barca being the only team besides PSG to get first-place votes.

Lamine Yamal (nine goals, 10 assists in all comps), Raphinha (14 goals, three assists) and Fermín López (five goals, three assists) are leading the way, but Flick is getting contributions up and down the roster, with Gabriel Jesus, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi making merry in the front-three rotation. Beyond that, Gerard Martín (24 years old) and Pau Cubarsí (19) have formed a classy central defensive partnership well beyond their years. It's too early to tell how Barca's season will ultimately pan out, but odds suggest they will slow down at some point from their 4.36 goals-per-game mark. A tough run of games to come -- after PSG, they have Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid in the next two to three weeks -- should be enlightening.

Until then, enjoy the show.

3. ARSENAL

- Previous rank: 2

- Games since MD1: defeated Sunderland 2-0, defeated Ipswich Town 4-2, lost 3-0 to Brighton, defeated Leeds 2-1, defeated Lille 3-0, defeated Nottingham Forest 1-0

- MD3 opponent: at Bayern Munich, Wednesday

Things are going pretty well for the Gunners this season, and it's fair to say they haven't lost the hunger for trophies after last season's triumphs; 10 wins from 11 games in all competitions speaks to that appetite. However, they are playing with their dinner a little bit -- Sunday's 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest saw Mikel Arteta's side generate just one shot on target from 75% possession -- and aren't finding things easy. Viktor Gyökeres has yet to open his 2026-27 account with zero goals from eight appearances, but the defense is as stingy as ever, and that's arguably the most important thing right now while they search for more consistency in attack.

We'll learn a lot from their midweek trip to Munich -- the Bavarians are 4-0-0 at home this season, outscoring opponents 23-2 in that span -- but regardless, our voters see them as the English team with the best chance of winning it all this season. It won't be easy.

4. BAYERN MUNICH

- Previous rank: 3

- Games since MD1: defeated Elversberg 2-1, defeated Union Berlin 7-0, drew 2-2 vs. Augsburg, drew 3-3 with Viking, defeated RB Leipzig 6-1

- MD3 opponent: vs. Arsenal, Wednesday

It's still too early to know what to make of Bayern. Our voters see them as a strong contender, ranking them no lower than fifth across all ballots; it makes sense, but they have looked a little less dominant in the early going this season than we're used to. Since thumping Bodo/Glimt 5-0 to open their Champions League account, they've shown their vulnerabilities. First, Manuel Neuer's goalkeeping howlers helped Augsburg to a 2-2 draw, and then Vincent Kompany's side turned in a rather dazed and confused performance in Norway, spotting tiny Viking FK a 2-0 lead, scoring three times in 17 second-half minutes to take the lead and then conceding a late equalizer after Michael Olise's reckless red card.

Olise, who picked up a yellow card for a foul and immediately received a second yellow for throwing the ball at the head of the guy he fouled, should have that out of his system now, and there's really little reason to panic yet. Sure, Harry Kane has only nine goals and six assists in his first 10 games of the season, but this team knows where to find that extra gear when needed. Will we see it against Arsenal this week?

5. MANCHESTER CITY

- Previous rank: 6

- Games since MD1: defeated Man United 1-0, defeated Norwich City 5-0, defeated Sunderland 5-3, defeated Liverpool 3-0, lost 4-2 vs. PSG, defeated Ipswich Town 3-2

- MD3 opponent: vs. AEK Athens, Tuesday

There are two overwhelming thoughts when it comes to Man City right now: This team is really, really good on the field, and yet, does it really matter?

While the independent panels review the appeals and sanction processes over their 114 Premier League financial charges, we can't really address the second thought above; however, credit to the players for continuing to tune out the considerable noise and keep getting impressive results, and to coach Enzo Maresca for not allowing the obvious concerns about the future from derailing his squad.

City are a perfect seven-for-seven in the Premier League and top the table by three points over Arsenal, and while PSG did humble them in the petrostate Royal Rumble last midweek, Erling Haaland (12 goals in 10 games) cannot be denied. Though they exist in an undeniable limbo, the big Norway striker keeps scoring.

6. REAL MADRID

- Previous rank: 5

- Games since MD1: defeated Rayo Vallecano 4-1, defeated Elche 3-2, lost 2-1 to Atletico Madrid, defeated Villarreal 1-0, defeated AS Roma 4-3

- MD3 opponent: vs. RB Leipzig, Wednesday

We knew that Jose Mourinho returning to the Bernabeu would be must-see TV, but maybe we still underestimated what a box-office event every matchday would be for Los Blancos. Derby defeat aside, they have been grinding out results with a heady, familiar blend of grit, petulance and sheer magic, mixing sublime goals with the drama we expect from a Mourinho-led team.

Last week was the perfect example: Just days after a 1-0 win over Villarreal in which Vinicius Jr. was sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair, they went to Rome and were in a 3-1 hole before scoring three times after the 81st minute to take all three points back home. Never a dull moment. Kylian Mbappé (11 goals and two assists in all competitions) is predictably leading the way, but they're getting contributions from everywhere in the squad, and Mourinho's razzle-dazzle in front of the media is helping keep the critics at bay.

It all feels so tenuous considering the combustible nature of Madrid in general, but it's great to watch.

7. LIVERPOOL

- Previous rank: 8

- Games since MD1: drew 0-0 vs. Fulham, defeated Tottenham 3-1, defeated Bournemouth 1-0, lost 3-0 vs. Man City, defeated LASK 6-3, defeated Brentford 2-1

- MD3 opponent: vs. Villarreal, Tuesday

It has been a case of one step forward, two steps back for Liverpool this season, as new manager Andoni Iraola is still searching for the right formula to make his star-studded (but thin) squad perform at its best. Imparting his teachings was always going to take time, but there is still a lot to be happy about if you're a Reds fan: Bradley Barcola has impressed in Champions League play, scoring a hat trick against LASK; Alexander Isak is back from injury; and the defensive pairing of Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk has been quietly impressive.

Florian Wirtz remains frustratingly enigmatic, mind you, and a possible long-term injury for Dominik Szoboszlai is a real loss for a midfield without an identity. (Look to youth prospect Trey Nyoni for more minutes in the holding midfielder role.) But for now, our voters see them as a credible challenger in the chasing pack considering how Champions League games tend to be a little more open and opponents less aggressive than in the Premier League. The added space and time on the ball should give Wirtz, Barcola, Cody Gakpo & Co. more opportunities to impress, and they'll need to against Villarreal before a brutal run of league fixtures (Brighton and Arsenal at Anfield, Crystal Palace away).

8. ATLÉTICO MADRID

- Previous rank: 9

- Games since MD1: defeated Real Sociedad 3-0, defeated Osasuna 4-0, defeated Real Madrid 2-1, defeated Alaves 2-0, defeated Man United 2-0, defeated Espanyol 1-0

- MD3 opponent: at VfB Stuttgart, Tuesday

Don't look now, but Diego Simeone's side might be one of the most in-form teams in Europe right now? Signature wins over crosstown rivals Real and a confident win over Manchester United in Champions League Matchday 2 have the Rojiblancos feeling good as we hurtle toward Halloween.

A 7-1-1 record in LaLiga sees them second above Real for now, with a big game against Barcelona ahead, but they're a scary prospect in their own right. Álex Baena (five goals, three assists) is leading the way statistically, but loanee Jonathan David has settled in brilliantly up front, Cristian Romero is a perfect bruiser for Simeone's uncompromising defense (though he is hurt right now), and Julián Álvarez is wrapping up his image-rehabilitation tour following all the transfer links to Barcelona over the summer.

With a winnable run of games before they welcome Barcelona on Nov. 8, our voters fancy Atletico to make a deep run in this competition.

9. INTER MILAN

- Previous rank: 7

- Games since MD1: defeated Udinese 5-3, drew 2-2 vs. AS Roma, defeated Parma 3-0, lost 4-3 vs. Club Brugge, defeated Bologna 3-1

- MD3 opponent: vs. Shakhtar Donetsk, Wednesday

It's hard to know what to make of the Italian champions, who are simultaneously at the top of Serie A with six wins and a draw while also being outside the Champions League top 24 following two defeats from two games. Their error-prone defending has hurt them against Real Madrid and Club Brugge in European play, but it's still early in the campaign, and the league phase format leaves plenty of room for big clubs to have a wobble and still advance. Doing it without the injured Lautaro Martínez over the next few weeks is another obstacle, but manager Cristian Chivu has the nous to figure it out.

10. ASTON VILLA

- Previous rank: N/R

- Games since MD1: lost 2-1 vs. Nottingham Forest, defeated Coventry City 3-1, defeated Tottenham 3-2, drew 2-2 vs. Brentford, defeated Fenerbahce 6-0, defeated Newcastle United 1-0

- MD3 opponent: vs. Viking, Wednesday

Last but not least are Villa, who are thriving in Europe (two wins from two games) despite finding themselves in the bottom half of the Premier League in the early going. Unai Emery's magic hasn't run out yet; after another summer of key players leaving, a new-look side is percolating nicely. Johan Manzambi and Nico Jackson are an exciting new attacking duo capable of creativity and goals, John McGinn's work rate is a template for teammates to follow, and new keeper Zion Suzuki is coming off two straight clean sheets.

It's not pretty, but it's working.

ALSO RECEIVING VOTES

Sporting CP, Borussia Dortmund, Real Betis, AS Roma, VfB Stuttgart, Manchester United, Como.

VOTERS

stories.headline: MLB qualifying offer for free agents rises to $23.15M, up 5.1% from last year
stories.summary: The price of a qualifying offer for this year's major league free agents rose 5.1% to $23.15 million from $22,025,000.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The price of a qualifying offer for this year's major league free agents rose 5.1% to $23.15 million from $22,025,000.

The figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts this year. The price dropped by $100,000 to $17.8 million in 2019, then rose to $18.9 million in 2020, fell $500,000 in 2021 and rose to $19.65 million in 2022, $20,325,000 in 2023 and $21.05 million in 2024.

Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season, and only 18 of 157 offers have been accepted.

A free agent can be made a qualifying offer only if he has been with the same team continuously since opening day and has never received a qualifying offer before.

Among the top players who can become free agents after the World Series and are eligible to receive qualifying offers are Seattle outfielder Randy Arozarena, New York Yankees left-hander David Bednar, Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh second baseman Brandon Lowe, San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon, Baltimore left-hander Trevor Rogers and Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki.

A record four players accepted last year from among the 13 who received offers: Chicago Cubs left-hander Shota Imanaga, Milwaukee right-hander Brandon Woodruff, New York Yankees outfielder Trent Grisham and Detroit second baseman Gleyber Torres.

Other potential free agents ineligible for qualifying offers this offseason include Philadelphia second baseman Luis Arraez, Baltimore right-hander Chris Bassitt, New York Mets third baseman Bo Bichette, Arizona right-hander Zac Gallen, San Diego right-hander Michael King, Padres left-hander Robbie Ray, Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Tarik Skubal and Toronto outfielder George Springer.

Bichette and King must decide on player options.

A qualifying offer can be made through the fifth day after the World Series, and a player has a week after that to accept.

If a team makes a qualifying offer to a player who signs a major league contract with another club before the amateur draft, his former club would receive a draft pick as compensation at the end of the first round or at the end of competitive balance round B. The placement depends on the amount of the new contract and the revenue-sharing and luxury tax status of the team losing the player.

Qualifying offers began at $13.3 million. Other players who accepted are Baltimore catcher Matt Wieters, Houston outfielder Colby Rasmus and Dodgers left-hander Brett Anderson ($15.8 million for 2016); Mets second baseman Neil Walker and Philadelphia right-hander Jeremy Hellickson ($17.2 million for 2017); Dodgers left-hander Hyun Jin Ryu ($17.9 million for 2019); Chicago White Sox first baseman José Abreu and Minnesota right-hander Jake Odorizzi ($17.8 million for 2020); San Francisco right-hander Kevin Gausman and Mets right-hander Marcus Stroman ($18.9 million for 2021); Giants first baseman Brandon Belt ($18.4 million for 2022; Texas left-hander Martín Pérez and Giants outfielder Joc Pederson ($19.65 million for 2023); and Cincinnati Reds right-hander Nick Martinez ($21.05 million for 2025).

stories.headline: Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili joins rare list of trilogy bouts at UFC 333
stories.summary: ESPN categorizes all 19 of the UFC's trilogies ahead of Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili 3 at UFC 333 on Saturday.
stories.body:
When men's bantamweight champion Petr Yan and former champion Merab Dvalishvili fight in the UFC 333 co-main event on Saturday in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, it will be their third meeting, completing the promotion's 20th trilogy.

This weekend's headliners, featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski and undefeated challenger Movsar Evloev, will square off for the first time, but Volkanovski has already been part of a UFC trilogy. His threepeat with Max Holloway several years ago played out far differently from what will unfold in the UFC 333 co-main. That's guaranteed. (Read on to find out why.)

How fitting is it that Saturday's event is numbered 333, a coincidental acknowledgment that when the UFC deals out three of a kind, the fans end up with a winning hand. Usually.

Trilogies come in all shapes with all sizes. Many of the sport's biggest stars have been in one or more, yet at least one UFC three-fight series featured competitors newer fans probably haven't heard of. Some trilogies have had championship-level stakes in each fight, while others have been driven by nothing but a scornful rivalry that makes the fights feel no less consequential. A few trilogies have been one-sided and a couple have concluded without establishing who's better. We did the math.

Other MMA organizations have staged trilogies, and some have played out across multiple promotions, but this list sticks to the 19 all-UFC trilogies to date and sorts them by similarities and distinguishing factors.

Passing the torch
Trilogies in which the winner of the first fight was at the top of the sport, and by the third meeting the opponent was MMA's top fighter

Chuck Liddell vs. Randy Couture
Results:

UFC 43, June 6, 2003: Couture def. Liddell (TKO3) for interim light heavyweight title
UFC 52, April 16, 2005: Liddell def. Couture (KO1) for light heavyweight title
UFC 57, Feb. 4, 2006: Liddell def. Couture (KO2) for light heavyweight title

Notable: In the lead-up to their second meeting, Liddell and Couture coached against each other on the inaugural season of "The Ultimate Fighter," the reality show UFC CEO Dana White often credits with keeping the UFC in business. Through their TV appearances and contrasting fighting styles and personalities, Liddell and Couture helped catapult MMA toward the sports mainstream. Couture is one of just three fighters (along with Tito Ortiz and Matt Hughes) to compete in two UFC trilogies -- this one and a trio of fights with Vitor Belfort.

Georges St-Pierre vs. Matt Hughes
Results:

UFC 50, Oct. 22, 2004: Hughes def. St-Pierre (Sub1) for welterweight title
UFC 65, Nov. 18, 2006: St-Pierre def. Hughes (TKO2) for welterweight title
UFC 79, Dec. 29, 2007: St-Pierre def. Hughes (Sub2) for interim welterweight title

Notable: This is the only UFC trilogy to feature multiple submission finishes. Hughes won by armbar at UFC 50, and St-Pierre ended the trilogy at UFC 79 by submitting Hughes, also by armbar. When the fighters were standing, though, GSP dominated. In their second meeting, he outstruck Hughes 49-10 with two knockdowns. In the third fight, it was 97-10.

A stunning start ... and finish
Trilogies that began with a shocking KO upset, followed by the KO victim scoring two dominant wins

Cain Velasquez vs. Junior Dos Santos
Results:

UFC on Fox, Nov. 12, 2011: Dos Santos def. Velasquez (KO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 155, Dec. 29, 2012: Velasquez def. Dos Santos (UD) for heavyweight title
UFC 166, Oct. 19, 2013: Velasquez def. Dos Santos (TKO5) for heavyweight title

Notable: The first fight lasted barely a minute, as Dos Santos essentially won by one-punch knockout. The rematch and trilogy fight dramatically swung the other way. Velasquez battered JDS for the full 25 minutes of their second meeting, as reflected by one judge awarding him two 10-8 rounds. Velasquez became the first UFC fighter to reach triple-figure significant strikes (111) and double-figure takedowns (11) in a single fight.

Stipe Miocic vs. Daniel Cormier
Results:

UFC 226, July 7, 2018: Cormier def. Miocic (KO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 241, Aug. 17, 2019: Miocic def. Cormier (TKO4) for heavyweight title
UFC 252, Aug. 15, 2020: Miocic def. Cormier (UD) for heavyweight title

Notable: Cormier was light heavyweight champion when he first faced Miocic, and by crushing the heavyweight king with an uppercut, Cormier became the second UFC champ to reign in two weight classes simultaneously. Miocic bounced back in the next two fights, and his victory in the third meeting tied him with Couture for the most UFC heavyweight title-fight wins, with six.

Back and forth (and back)
Trilogies in which the winner of the first fight lost the second, then won the third -- a rarity

Randy Couture vs. Vitor Belfort
Results:

UFC 15, Oct. 17, 1997: Couture def. Belfort (TKO1)
UFC 46, Jan. 31, 2004: Belfort def. Couture (TKO1) for light heavyweight title
UFC 49, Aug. 21, 2004: Couture def. Belfort (TKO3) for light heavyweight title

Notable: Entering the first fight, Belfort was 20 years old and 4-0 as a pro -- all knockouts of a minute, 17 seconds or faster. But Couture, 34, stopped his momentum cold. When they met again six years later, Belfort won in 49 seconds after his glove scraped Couture's eye, causing a corneal abrasion that prompted the cageside doctor to stop the fight. In the third fight, Couture brutalized Belfort for three rounds before that event's doctor had seen enough. This is the only UFC trilogy in which two fights ended by doctor's stoppage.

BJ Penn vs. Matt Hughes
Results:

UFC 46, Jan. 31, 2004: Penn def. Hughes (Sub1) for welterweight title
UFC 63, Sept. 23, 2006: Hughes def. Penn (TKO3) for welterweight title
UFC 123, Nov. 20, 2010: Penn def. Hughes (KO1)

Notable: After two unsuccessful bids for the lightweight championship, Penn moved up to welterweight and won the belt in a stunning upset, ending Hughes' two-year reign and 13-fight winning streak. After Hughes won the rematch to even the score, Penn completed the trilogy in style, knocking out Hughes in 21 seconds -- the fastest finish in a UFC trilogy.

You're just flexing now
Trilogies that ended in a 3-0 sweep

Tito Ortiz vs. Ken Shamrock
Results:

UFC 40, Nov. 12, 2002: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO3) for light heavyweight title
UFC 61, July 8, 2006: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO1)
UFC Ortiz vs. Shamrock 3, Oct. 10, 2006: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO1)

Notable: This trilogy is unmatched in its bitter animosity, for sure, and maybe even in one-sidedness. The feud grew out of the brash Ortiz defeating fighters from Shamrock's highly regarded Lion's Den gym, then mocking that team with vulgar gestures and custom T-shirts. Ortiz and Shamrock finally met at UFC 40 amid much anticipation, and the heated buildup drove a pay-per-view buy rate double what the UFC had ever seen.

Frankie Edgar vs. BJ Penn
Results:

UFC 112, April 10, 2010: Edgar def. Penn (UD) for lightweight title
UFC 118, Aug. 28, 2010: Edgar def. Penn (UD) for lightweight title
The Ultimate Fighter 19 Finale, July 6, 2014: Edgar def. Penn (TKO3)

Notable: Penn, who had not lost a lightweight bout in eight years, was a near 8-1 betting favorite in the first fight. Even after Edgar pulled off a narrow upset, he was still the underdog entering the rematch. He won that one more clearly with three 50-45 scorecards, then completed the trilogy with a knockout. Of the UFC's 19 trilogies, 11 have ended with a finish in the third fight. But only two -- both involving Edgar -- ended with a finish after two consecutive decisions. The other was Edgar's series with Gray Maynard.

Alexander Volkanovski vs. Max Holloway
Results:

UFC 245, Dec. 14, 2019: Volkanovski def. Holloway (UD) for featherweight title
UFC 251, July 11, 2020: Volkanovski def. Holloway (SD) for featherweight title
UFC 276, July 2, 2022: Volkanovski def. Holloway (UD) for featherweight title

Notable: Just because this trilogy ended 3-0 doesn't mean Volkanovski had it easy. In the second fight, Holloway knocked him down in each of the first two rounds, forcing the champ to play catch-up. Holloway made Volkanovski work the full five rounds in all three fights. At 75 minutes of total cage time, this is the UFC's longest trilogy.

Let's call it even
Trilogies that ended at 1-1, plus a draw

Frankie Edgar vs. Gray Maynard
Results:

UFC Fight Night, April 2, 2008: Maynard def. Edgar (UD)
UFC 125, Jan. 1, 2011: Maynard vs. Edgar for lightweight title ends in split draw
UFC 136, Oct. 8, 2011: Edgar def. Maynard (KO4) for lightweight title

Notable: The second meeting produced the greatest comeback and the most memorable draw in UFC history. Maynard knocked Edgar down three times in Round 1 while piling up a 47-10 edge in strikes landed. All three judges scored it 10-8, and Edgar was so rocked that he doesn't remember anything from the rounds that followed. He "missed" a great fight. The final meeting also began badly for Edgar, but this time his comeback built toward a late knockout that emphatically evened the score.

Valentina Shevchenko vs. Alexa Grasso
Results:

UFC 285, March 4, 2023: Grasso def. Shevchenko (Sub4) for women's flyweight title
Noche UFC, Sept. 16, 2023: Shevchenko vs. Grasso for women's flyweight title ends in split draw
UFC 306, Sept. 14, 2024: Shevchenko def. Grasso (UD) for women's flyweight title

Notable: The only women's trilogy in UFC history opened with a staggering upset, as Grasso capitalized on an ill-advised spinning attack by Shevchenko to seize control and quickly lock in a choke that ended the champ's six-year unbeaten run. Grasso narrowly held on to the title in a tightly contested second fight. Shevchenko dominated the third meeting, thanks to a change in strategy. Her grappling-heavy approach produced at least one takedown in each of the five rounds, 16 minutes of ground control and a trio of 50-45 scorecards.

Remember me?
Trilogies with at least seven years between fights

Dustin Poirier vs. Max Holloway
Results:

UFC 143, Feb. 4, 2012: Poirier def. Holloway (Sub1) for interim lightweight title
UFC 236, April 13, 2019: Poirier def. Holloway (UD)
UFC 318, July 19, 2025: Holloway def. Poirier (UD) for BMF title

Notable: The first fight was Holloway's UFC debut at 20 years old, and their final meeting 13 years later was Poirier's retirement fight. By winning that third bout, Holloway became the first fighter to win a UFC trilogy after losing the first two matchups.

Leon Edwards vs. Kamaru Usman
Results:

UFC on Fox, Dec. 19, 2015: Usman def. Edwards (UD)
UFC 278, Aug. 20, 2022: Edwards def. Usman (KO5) for welterweight title
UFC 268, March 18, 2023: Edwards def. Usman (MD) for welterweight title

Notable: Usman was 58 seconds from going up 2-0 in this series when an Edwards head kick out of nowhere changed everything. Usman had won 15 fights in a row and was on the verge of tying Anderson Silva's record for the longest UFC win streak at the time. Since that shocking defeat, he's gone 1-3, including another loss to Edwards.

No gold, just (a little) glory
Trilogies in which no championships were on the line

Sam Stout vs. Spencer Fisher
Results:

UFC 58, March 4, 2006: Stout def. Fisher (SD)
UFC Fight Night, June 12, 2007: Fisher def. Stout (UD)
UFC on FX, June 22, 2012: Stout def. Fisher (UD)

Notable: The first meeting was Stout's UFC debut, and apparently both fighters were just warming up. The rematch and trilogy fight each earned fight of the night bonuses. The third meeting had an added emotional element for Stout, as it was his first fight after the death of his coach and brother-in-law, Shawn Tompkins.

Forrest Griffin vs. Tito Ortiz
Results:

UFC 59, April 15, 2006: Ortiz def. Griffin (SD)
UFC 106, Nov. 21, 2009: Griffin def. Ortiz (SD)
UFC 148, July 7, 2012: Griffin def. Ortiz (UD)

Notable: Both competitors were 205-pound champions, just not during any of their three meetings. All three fights happened after Ortiz's title reign from 2000 to 2003. The first fight was before Griffin became champ in 2008, and the other two were after he lost the belt later that same year. The trilogy fight was Griffin's career finale and Ortiz's final UFC appearance.

Charles Oliveira vs. Nik Lentz
Results:

UFC on Versus, June 26, 2011: Oliveira vs. Lentz ends in no contest
UFC Fight Night, May 30, 2015: Oliveira def. Lentz (Sub3)
UFC Fight Night, May 18, 2019: Oliveira def. Lentz (TKO2)

Notable: The first bout appeared to end with an Oliveira rear-naked choke in Round 2, but the Pennsylvania State Athletic Commission ruled that Oliveira had landed an illegal knee and overturned the result to a no-contest. The bout earned both men fight of the night bonuses, as did the second fight.

Dustin Poirier vs. Conor McGregor
Results:

UFC 178, Sept. 27, 2014: McGregor def. Poirier (TKO1)
UFC 257, Jan. 23, 2021: Poirier def. McGregor (TKO2)
UFC 264, July 10, 2021: Poirier def. McGregor (TKO1)

Notable: This rivalry could have fit in the "Remember me?" category because of the seven-year gap between the first and second bouts. But what truly makes this trilogy stand apart from all others is McGregor's star power. He headlined the seven highest-selling pay-per-views in UFC history, and only his bouts with Khabib Nurmagomedov and Nate Diaz outsold his two meetings with Poirier in 2021. McGregor suffered the first two knockout losses of his MMA career in those bouts, the second finish coming by doctor's stoppage after he broke his left tibia and fibula.

Three is not enough?
The only UFC tetralogy -- plus 75% of another

Brandon Moreno vs. Deiveson Figueiredo
Results:

UFC 256, Dec. 12, 2020: Moreno vs. Figueiredo for men's flyweight title ends in majority draw
UFC 263, June 12, 2021: Moreno def. Figueiredo (Sub3) for men's flyweight title
UFC 270, Jan. 22, 2022: Figueiredo def. Moreno (UD) for men's flyweight title
UFC 283, Jan. 21, 2023: Moreno def. Figueiredo (TKO3) for men's flyweight title

Notable: These two flyweights squeezed in four fights over 25 months, faster than many two-fight series. Moreno and Figueiredo each produced heart-pounding moments throughout the four fights, and together they landed exactly 700 strikes. The second fight represented a memorable accomplishment for Moreno when he became the first Mexico-born UFC champion.

Tim Sylvia vs. Andrei Arlovski
Results:

UFC 51, Feb. 5, 2005: Arlovski def. Sylvia (Sub1) for interim heavyweight title
UFC 59, April 15, 2006: Sylvia def. Arlovski (TKO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 61, July 8, 2006: Sylvia def. Arlovski (UD) for heavyweight title
One FC 5, Aug. 31, 2012: Sylvia vs. Arlovski ends no contest in One Championship

Notable: The first fight lasted 47 seconds, with Arlovski's quick knockdown leading to a leg-lock finish. Arlovski nearly repeated the feat in the rematch, dropping Sylvia halfway through Round 1. But after a wobbly Sylvia got back to his feet and Arlovski moved in for a finish, Sylvia caught him with a short uppercut to even the score. Their final UFC meeting turned into a tactical, tentative sparring session, as one might expect from a matchup where each fighter had already felt the other's power. Also as expected, the ornery crowd was unimpressed.

stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at United States GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli, it's too late

- Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant Singapore drive

- Hamilton calls Singapore strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027?
